title: Page 1
summary: A 19 April 1974 CIA memo to the Director of Central Intelligence alerts him to an issue likely raised by Secretary Rush at lunch. A SKYLAB mission inadvertently photographed a location that had been specifically excluded. Interagency review has no agreement: DoD elements (USAF, NRO, JCS, ISA) want it withheld, while NASA and State favor release to the Sioux Falls repository. A position paper is forthcoming; most officials think the decision belongs at agency head level. Classification of the platform and imagery must be reviewed first.

title: Page 2
summary: The text is a fragment from a declassified CIA document (Approved for Release 2004). It raises two points: complex UN issues concerning United States policies on space-based imagery, and whether a photograph can be withheld without leaking. Marked CONFIDENTIAL, with redacted content.

title: Page 3
summary: This is a scanned, OCR-garbled CIA routing and approval slip (Approved For Release 2004/10/12, CIA-RDP80M01048A000800210008-5). It lists action and info routing boxes for numbered offices (e.g., ASST/DCI, AO/DCI, EX/S&C, D/P, GC, DDM&S, DDO), a suspense date, and handwritten remarks that are largely illegible. The text is too degraded to summarize its substantive content reliably.

title: Page 4
summary: A declassified CIA memo (Approved for Release 2004/10/12, CIA-RDP80M01048A000800210008-5) addressed to Mr. Colby says the attached item was hand-carried in for his lunch with Deputy Secretary Rush that day. The text is mostly OCR residue with a form number (Form 101, replacing 10-101, dated 1 Aug 54) and a partial 1974 date stamp.
